rationale: Distinct from the 'sinew' sense already in glossary. Here in the zodiacal melothesia (Aries=head, Taurus=neck/shoulders) the term names the neck. ⲙⲟⲩⲧ in Coptic supports both senses; context here selects 'neck.'
Lycopolitan body-part term, = Sahidic ϭⲛⲁⲩϩ/ϭⲃⲟⲓ 'arm.' Used twice on this page (lines 4, 22) in the zodiacal mapping where Gemini = the two arms — standard melothesia.
Lycopolitan body-part term. Mapped to Cancer in this kephalaion's body-zodiac correspondence — canonical position for the breast/thorax in melothesia. Possibly cognate with ⲙⲉⲥⲧⲛⲍⲏⲧ family.
Lycopolitan ⲝ for ϫ; = ϫⲓⲥⲉ here as body-part 'loin.' Mapped to Libra in conjunction with hips — standard.
Lycopolitan plural of ϣⲡⲁⲧ 'thigh, hip.' Component of Libra in this melothesia. Standard Coptic body-part.

While 'bosom' fits other contexts (cf. accumulated entry 'their bosom' = 'innermost'), in this strict melothesia ⲕⲟⲩⲟⲩⲛϥ̄ corresponds to Scorpio = the genital/groin region in canonical zodiacal anatomy.

Body-part term filling the Sagittarius slot (between groin and knees) in the melothesia. Sagittarius governs the thighs in classical/Hellenistic astrology. Etymology uncertain — possibly Lyc. for a thigh-term.
Lycopolitan ⲡⲉⲧ = Sahidic ⲡⲁⲧ 'knee.' Mapped to Capricorn — standard melothesia.
Likely Lyc. for ⲥⲛⲁⲩϩ 'two tendons/sinews,' here used of the paired calf-tendons. Mapped to Aquarius (= calves/shins in classical melothesia).
Lycopolitan body-part term in possessed form (ⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ 'his leg/foot'). Construction ⲥⲛϩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ = 'calves of his leg(s).'
Lycopolitan body-part term, likely = Sahidic ⲱⲡ or related. Mapped to Pisces (= feet) in canonical melothesia: 'the soles of his feet are the Fish.'
Coptic ⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'foundation.' In context 'head against the foundation,' designates the lower terminus opposing the head — the body's vertical span.
Distinct from ⲧⲡⲉ 'heaven/above.' Here = Lyc. ⲧⲏⲡⲉ 'ankle, extremity.' Confirmed by symmetric construction in lines 18 ('from head down to his ⲧⲡⲉ') and 27 ('from his ⲧⲡⲉ up to his head').
Obscure body-part term. In the right-half enumeration of zodiac-correspondences, fills the Aries slot (= head equivalent on the right side). Possibly 'temple' or 'right brow.' Confidence low.
Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲍⲃⲉ = Sahidic ⲛⲁϩⲃ 'shoulder' (already in accumulated vocabulary). Singular form attested here in line 21-22.
Coptic ⲥⲡⲓⲣ 'rib, side.' Body-part term used in the right/left half-mapping for Cancer/Scorpio. In the full-body schema breast/groin; in lateral schema becomes side/rib.
Body-part term modified by ⲡⲥⲁ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲛⲉⲙ 'right side of.' Mapped to Virgo. Possibly = ⲛⲁϩⲧⲉ 'innards' or related anatomical plural. Confidence moderate.

Body-part term in left-half enumeration mapped (with ⲟⲗⲱⲧⲉ) to Sagittarius = thigh. Sahidic ⲕⲓⲃⲉ usually = 'breast' but Manichaean Lyc. usage here clearly anatomical-lower. Possibly a Lyc. extension to thigh/loin region.
Coptic ⲟⲗⲱⲧⲉ 'kidney' (cf. Sah. ⲟⲗⲱⲧⲉ ⲡϫⲟⲧ). In paired Sagittarius-correspondence (= thigh region), kidneys/loins fit anatomically.

Body-part term mapped to Capricorn(?) — wait, Capricorn = knees in standard. But here in left-half schema where line 30 restoration suggests Capricorn slot, ⲕⲁⲗⲁⲛⲕⲉⲍ may shift. Possibly Greek κάλαγξ-related. Confidence low.
Obscure compound. Position in left-half enumeration before Scorpio (left-rib) requires the Libra/hip slot. Possible analysis: ⲧ-ϩⲃⲟⲩⲣ-(ⲁ)ⲥⲟⲩⲛ 'the inner-left' or similar. Confidence low.
Greek δίδυμος 'twin' transcribed in Coptic. The δ→ⲇ and intervocalic shift give ⲇⲁⲩⲙⲟⲥ. Standard zodiacal designation.
Greek ὑδροχόος 'water-pourer' (Aquarius) with Lyc. ⲍ for ὑ and ⲭ for χ. Standard zodiacal name preserving the active 'pouring' verbal force.
Greek αἰγόκερως 'goat-horn' (Capricorn). Lyc. orthography ⲁⲓⲣ for αἰγ-. Standard zodiacal designation.
Greek τοξότης 'archer' (Sagittarius). Standard.
Greek ζυγός 'yoke, balance' (Libra). Standard zodiacal name.
Greek κριός 'ram' (Aries). Standard.
Greek ταῦρος 'bull' (Taurus). Standard.
Greek καρκίνος 'crab' (Cancer). Standard.
Greek λέων 'lion' (Leo). Standard.
Greek παρθένος 'virgin' (Virgo). Distinct from cosmic 'Virgin of Light' usage; here purely zodiacal.
Greek σκορπίος 'scorpion' (Scorpio). Standard.
Greek ἰχθύς 'fish' — in zodiacal use, Pisces. Singular form here functioning collectively for the constellation.
